logp.method_description: The lipophilicity (log Po/w values) of one probe indicates its relative solubility in oil and water, which is one of the major factors for probe to permeate cell membranes.20 Herein, the lipophilicity of complexes Ir1–Ir4 has been measured by the partition coefficient in octanol/water through a classical method in accordance with the literature.21 The log Po/w values of complexes Ir1–Ir4 are listed in Table S3 (ESI†). Considering the hydrophilic environment around cells and the phospholipid layer of the cellular membrane, amphiphilic complexes are the best choice for cellular probes. The hydrophilic part is needed for the solubility in the water while the lipophilic part helps the cellular probe to enter the living cells. The lipophilicity of all complexes changes from hydrophilic to hydrophobic with log Po/w changing from 0.05 (complex Ir4) to 0.31 (complex Ir2) due to the different cyclometalated ligands. These log Po/w values reveal that complexes Ir1– Ir4 possess amphiphilic character. Thus, all complexes can be dissolved in water as well as taken up by cells.
